target_customer: Working professionals and career switchers in Europe paying for online data, AI, marketing and programming courses, plus government funded training buyers
problem: Traditional education and bootcamps are slow, expensive and poorly matched to job market needs for people who work full time.
business_model: Tuition for online cohort programs with 1 on 1 mentoring, including deferred payment options; government training funds; EU grants

founders.name: Lukas Kaminskis
founders.background_notes: Company about page: led Turing College and earlier Turing Society since 2017. Not listed on the YC page profile.

founders.name: Tomas Moska
founders.background_notes: YC page: self taught, became CTO of an early startup at 20 (unnamed).

founders.name: Benas Sidlauskas
previous_startups: Global tech network for the Lithuanian diaspora
A bootstrapped startup studio at 350k dollars annual revenue

competitors.name: Lambda School (BloomTech)
competitors.what: Online tech bootcamp with income share agreements

competitors.name: Springboard
competitors.what: Online data science bootcamp at 7,500 dollars upfront
competitors.traction_then: listed as most affordable data science bootcamp in a 2021 comparison

competitors.name: Flatiron School and General Assembly
competitors.what: Established bootcamps priced around 15,000 dollars upfront

technical_complexity.rationale: Learning platform, mentor matching and curriculum operations; the AI personalization claimed later is more complex but was not the 2020 core.

defensibility.rationale: Courses and mentors can be copied; advantages are local regulatory approvals, funded training eligibility and a mentor network.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying Turing College; it instead acquired a UK apprenticeship provider in 2025.

market_need_then: Demand for data science and AI reskilling among working adults in Europe in 2020 and 2021, with few Baltic or European online options and Tech.eu coverage of a launch promising well paid jobs.

branding.name_origin: The company's blog says it is named after Alan Turing for his codebreaking work and his ideas about thinking machines.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical, international, positioned against traditional education

branding.brand_signature: Alan Turing name and CS50 partnership
branding.community_and_virality: Grew from the Turing Society student community; claims 3,000 plus learners from 69 countries.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong regional name recognition from the first Lithuanian YC startup coverage and a community lineage, but a 2021 blog questioned use of Turing's name without the estate and the name is shared with other Turing companies.

outcome_analysis: Turing College grew from a student community into a funded Lithuanian online school, was the first Lithuanian YC company, raised a 2020 initial round and a 1.05M dollar seed in 2021, won a 2.5M euro EIC grant in 2024 and bought Boom Training in 2025. It is still Active with about 50 staff. Capital raised is modest, so success rests on execution, European reach and public funding rather than venture scale.
notes: The 2020 round is reported as 1.4M dollars by ain.ua and as 1.2M euro by CEE Legal Matters, which names Startup Wise Guys and Motieka as investors; kept at the 1.4M dollar figure and flagged as conflicting. The 2024 EIC grant was 2.5M euro, left null in dollars. CB Insights lists a Tesonet Accelerator round dated October 2023, single source, not recorded. Total raised ranges from 2.5M to 3.8M dollars by source. The competitor source is a 2021 listicle with no month. The YC page lists three co-founders including an unprofiled Lukas; the about page names Lukas Kaminskis as CEO.
